Import DHS microdata you have downloaded

Source: R/import.R
bdhs_import.Rd

Registers DHS data files in the local bdhs data store so that bdhs_read() can load any round and recode in one line. Point it at the files, zip archives or folders you downloaded from the DHS Program: files are identified with bdhs_identify_file() whatever they are called, folders are searched recursively and zip archives (also nested ones, such as the bulk "STATA_BD_..." downloads) are unpacked to a temporary folder.

Usage

bdhs_import(
  path,
  copy = TRUE,
  format = c("auto", "parquet", "dta"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Paths to data files (.dta, .sav, .sas7bdat), zip archives or folders.

copy

Keep a copy in the data store (TRUE, default) or register the files in place (FALSE).

format

Storage format for copies: "auto" (Parquet if arrow is installed, otherwise the original file), "parquet" or "dta" (a byte-for-byte copy of the original Stata, SPSS or SAS file).

overwrite

Replace datasets that are already registered from a different file (or re-import identical ones).

quiet

If TRUE, do not print the import summary. Warnings are still shown.

Value

The registry rows of the imported datasets, invisibly: columns survey_id, recode, file_stem, format, path, linked, source_path, md5, n_rows, n_cols, imported_at and bdhs_version.

Details

When the same dataset is found in several formats, the Stata version is preferred, then SPSS, then SAS. Files that were already imported (same MD5 checksum) are skipped, as are derived or pooled files (several rounds appended together, or with variables that are not in the DHS recode). If the file registered with the same checksum no longer exists (it was moved or deleted), the file is registered again from its new location.

Files whose name and content disagree (for example a children's recode saved as BDIR81FL.DTA), and renamed files that their content does not confirm as Bangladesh DHS recode files, are not imported; see bdhs_identify_file().

Files inside the data directory are not imported, except the zips that bdhs_download(import = FALSE) keeps in its downloads folder. Only one R session at a time can import into (or bdhs_forget() from) a data directory; another session waits up to a minute (option bdhs.lock_timeout, in seconds) for it to finish.

With copy = TRUE (default) a copy is kept in bdhs_data_dir(): with format = "auto" it is converted to Parquet when the arrow package is installed (much faster to read selected columns; variable labels, value labels and Stata extended missing values are kept), otherwise the original file is copied. With copy = FALSE files are registered where they are and nothing is copied; files inside zip archives are always copied.

DHS microdata are licensed to you personally and must not be shared. bdhs never uploads or shares them, and warns when the data directory is inside a git repository or a cloud-synchronised folder.

See also

Other data store: bdhs_data_dir(), bdhs_download(), bdhs_forget(), bdhs_identify_file(), bdhs_inventory(), bdhs_read(), bdhs_read_file(), bdhs_sitrep()

Examples

# Synthetic files with DHS names, for illustration only
dl <- file.path(tempdir(), "dhs-downloads")
dir.create(dl, showWarnings = FALSE)
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR", n_clusters = 4, households = 3),
                 file.path(dl, "BDKR81FL.DTA"))
haven::write_dta(bdhs_simulate(2022, "HR", n_clusters = 4, households = 3),
                 file.path(dl, "BDHS2022HR.dta"))
bdhs_import(dl, format = "dta")
#> ✔ Imported 2 datasets into /tmp/RtmpCna1OW/bdhs-import-example:
#> • BD2022DHS HR (BDHR81FL): copied (.dta), 12 rows x 18 variables
#> • BD2022DHS KR (BDKR81FL): copied (.dta), 2 rows x 49 variables
bdhs_inventory(2022)
